Oak of Moreh
MOH-reh
proper noun
Hebrew Moreh, “teacher” or “instruction,” from a root to teach or point out; the plain or oak of Moreh at Shechem where Abram built his first altar in Canaan. Distinct from the hill of Moreh in the vale of Jezreel.

Biblical Definition

When Abram first entered the land of promise, he came to Shechem: “And Abram passed through the land unto the place of Sichem, unto the plain of Moreh. And the Canaanite was then in the land” (Gen 12:6). At this plain, or oak, of Moreh — a name that speaks of teaching — the LORD appeared to him and said, Unto thy seed will I give this land; and there Abram built his first altar unto the LORD who had appeared to him. It is worth marking the words that stand beside the altar: “the Canaanite was then in the land.” Abram raised his worship in the midst of enemy territory, upon no possession of his own, on the bare word of promise alone. He had not one foot of the land in hand, yet he built an altar and called upon the name of the LORD. Here is the first altar of the pilgrim faith. It teaches that true worship rests not upon the believer’s present possession but upon God’s promise; that the saint may set up the worship of God in the very country of his foes; and that faith takes God at His word before it sees the inheritance. Moreh signifies instruction, and this oak instructs the church still: build your altar on the promise, though the Canaanite be in the land. This is not the hill of Moreh in Jezreel where Gideon camped, but the oak of Abram’s first worship.

Webster 1828 Definition

The plain or oak of Moreh at Shechem where Abram built his first altar in Canaan though the Canaanite was in the land (Gen 12:6); the first altar of the pilgrim faith. Distinct from the hill of Moreh in Jezreel.

OAK OF MOREH, the plain of Moreh at Shechem in Canaan.

The name signifies teaching or instruction.

There Abram built his first altar to the LORD (Gen 12:6).

He worshipped though the Canaanite was then in the land.

Distinct from the hill of Moreh in the vale of Jezreel.

Key Scripture

Gen 12:6 — "And Abram passed through the land unto the place of Sichem, unto the plain of Moreh. And the Canaanite was then in the land."

Deu 11:30 — "Are they not on the other side Jordan, by the way where the sun goeth down, in the land of the Canaanites, which dwell in the champaign over against Gilgal, beside the plains of Moreh?"

Heb 11:16 — "But now they desire a better country, that is, an heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to be called their God: for he hath prepared for them a city."

1Pe 2:11 — "Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul;"

Modern Corruption

The oak of Abram’s first altar at Shechem; it recovers the boldness of the pilgrim faith that worships on the promise even in the enemy’s land.

expand to see more

The plain of Moreh is chiefly confused, not corrupted — taken for the hill of Moreh in Jezreel where Gideon encamped. This entry attends the Genesis oak of Abram’s first altar, a different place bearing the same name of instruction.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the boldness of the pilgrim faith, which builds its altar upon the promise of God even where the enemy holds the land. Abram possessed nothing but the word, yet he worshipped. So the church, a stranger and pilgrim in a world not yet subdued to Christ, sets up the pure worship of God on the ground of promise, waiting for the inheritance sure to come.

Hebrew Roots

Moreh comes from yarah, to throw, point out, or teach; hence Moreh means teacher or instruction, and this oak of Moreh is the place of teaching.

Moreh — from yarah, to point out or teach.

Hence Moreh signifies teacher or instruction.

Rendered plain or oak of Moreh at Shechem (Gen 12:6).

Named again as a landmark of the covenant charge (Deu 11:30).

Not the hill of Moreh in Jezreel of Judges 7.
